subject: Metering retry behavior and billing fallbacks for AWS Marketplace SaaS
messages:
From: Liz Harper <liz.harper@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on missed metering events & retries (Acme production)

Ben —

Quick question as we're preparing for go-live next week: we saw a handful of missing usage reports during a brief network outage last month. If Redwood's SaaS agent misses a metering callback, what exact retry policy does AWS Marketplace expect? Specifically:

- How long will Redwood attempt to resend a usage record before it's considered permanently lost?
- Do you have a fallback path we can use to ensure customers aren't billed incorrectly (e.g., bulk backfill via fulfillment API + invoice reconciliation)?
- In cases where usage is duplicated after a retry, what's your dedupe guarantee and window?

We have a contractual clause in the draft SLA about dispute windows and refunds; I'd like to align the technical behavior with billing expectations so finance isn't surprised. Attached a short log excerpt and our draft SLA clause for reference.

Attachments: metering-spec-v1.pdf (pdf), acme-sla-attachment.pdf (pdf)

Appreciate the quick turnaround — can hop on a 30-min sync if that's easier.

— Liz
Director, Cloud Platform
Acme Corp
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Liz Harper <liz.harper@acme.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on missed metering events & retries (Acme production)

Hi Liz — thanks for the details and the attachments. Short answers up front, then proposed next steps: 

- Retry policy: Redwood will attempt exponential backoff retries for missed usage submissions for up to 72 hours by default; after that we surface the event to ops for manual backfill. For Marketplace fulfillment we also queue a guaranteed delivery path for 7 days before marking as failed (we can configure to 30 days for enterprise tenants).
- Fallback/backfill: We support bulk backfill via the AWS Marketplace SaaS fulfillment API; we'll prepare a reconciled CSV and run against the entitlement/usage endpoint — ops will validate before finalizing billing.
- Dedup: Our ingestion layer includes a 14-day dedupe window keyed by customer-id + usage-id; retries that arrive within that window are ignored. We can extend to 30 days on request.

I've looped in Priyom (marketplace integration) and Naomi (billing ops) to confirm the defaults and surface any constraints from Marketplace. Karthik is on copy for legal/billing policy alignment. 

Proposed next step: 30-minute sync Monday to walk through your SLA clause and lock-in retry windows and refund flow. Is 10am PT Monday OK?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liz Harper <liz.harper@acme.com>, Tom Cheng <tom.cheng@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Question on missed metering events & retries (Acme production)

Ben / Naomi / Karthik / Liz —

Following up with the engineering details. I pulled together a short draft of the retry/resilience behavior and an operational playbook (attached: metering-retry-draft.md). Key points: 

1) Local buffering: the SaaS agent persists usage events to a local, encrypted queue and will attempt immediate submit; failures trigger exponential backoff (base 30s, max 1hr) for the first 72 hours.

2) Secondary queue: a durable fan-out queue (SQS) receives all events and acts as a 7-day replay window to call the Marketplace entitlement/usage API. This is our guaranteed delivery path. If you want 30 days we can opt into longer retention, but note increased storage and audit surface.

3) Idempotency & dedupe: we adhere to an idempotency token that is customer-id + event-uuid; AWS Marketplace accepts idempotent usage submissions but brokers can still accept duplicates in edge cases. We run a dedupe pass at ingestion and mark any collisions for manual review. Typical false positives are <0.05% on high-volume tests.

4) Backfill runbook: when we detect a gap >0.5% over a 24-hour window, ops will prepare a reconciled CSV, run a dry-run against the fulfillment API, then execute after you (Acme) sign off. We'll provide a time-limited preview link before applying.

5) Monitoring & alerts: we'll add a per-customer alert that triggers at 0.2% missed-event rate over 6 hours for high-SLA customers (like Acme).

I've included links in the doc to the Marketplace fulfillment API endpoints and an example dry-run output.

Quoted for context:
> On Fri, 18 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700 Liz Harper <liz.harper@acme.com> wrote:
> Ben —
> Quick question as we're preparing for go-live next week: we saw a handful of missing usage reports during a brief network outage last month...

Attachments: metering-retry-draft.md (text)

Questions for Naomi: is our proposed backfill cadence acceptable from a billing/finance perspective (dry-run -> ops sign-off -> execute)? Also, any concerns with extending the dedupe window to 30 days for Acme?

— Priyom
Senior Integrations Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liz Harper <liz.harper@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:06:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Question on missed metering events & retries (Acme production)

Thanks Priyom — this looks good. A few billing notes from our side: 

- Dry-run -> ops sign-off -> execute is the right pattern. Finance wants the dry-run output (CSV) to include both the original event timestamps and consolidated billed-period buckets so auditors can reconcile quickly.
- Refund/dispute window: per our standard Marketplace engagement, customers have a 90-day dispute window after invoice issuance. For Acme, legal is asking for a 120-day window in the contract; we can support that but will need explicit notification in the billing UI and the reporting exports.
- Duplicate charge protection: if a duplicate usage submission slips through and results in an overcharge, we will automatically flag and create a credit memo once identified. We aim to detect and revert duplicates within 7 business days; if it's detected after invoice settlement, we'll issue a credit on the next invoice cycle unless the amount exceeds >$5k, in which case we expedite.

Operational asks for Priyom: include the invoice-id field in the dry-run output and surface a checksum column so finance can validate against our accounting exports. Also, please include a sample timeline for a backfill (dry-run -> sign-off -> execution -> reflected in invoices).

Thanks — Naomi
Head of Billing Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Liz Harper <liz.harper@acme.com>, Tom Cheng <tom.cheng@acme.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on missed metering events & retries (Acme production) — agreed next steps

Liz / Tom —

Thanks for the quick attention everyone. Quick summary and agreed next steps: 

1) Redwood defaults: 72-hour client retry window + 7-day guaranteed replay queue (can extend retention to 30 days if requested).
2) Deduplication: 14-day default, can be extended to 30 days for Acme; Priyom will add idempotency token details to the doc.
3) Backfill process: Priyom to produce dry-run CSV (includes invoice-id & checksum) by EOD Tuesday; Naomi will confirm sign-off process and expected invoice cycle impact.
4) Contract alignment: Karthik/legal to confirm language update for a 120-day dispute window and explicit reference to our backfill process in the SLA.
5) Schedule: 30-minute sync confirmed for Monday 10am PT (invite sent).

Links: AWS fulfillment console (https://console.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/fulfillment/12345), HubSpot record (https://redwood.company/sales/hubspot/ACME-123)

Best,
